protocol.writer_contention: connection A holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE while connection B attempts BEGIN IMMEDIATE
protocol.stale_snapshot: reader A begins and materializes value a; writer B commits value b; reader A rereads then attempts UPDATE without restarting its read transaction
protocol.checkpoint_blockage: reader holds a read snapshot while writer commits 200 one-row transactions; third connection attempts PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE), then repeats after reader release

claim_assessment.evidence: Second BEGIN IMMEDIATE failed with SQLITE_BUSY while first writer held the write transaction.

claim_assessment.claim: A WAL reader retains its old snapshot and cannot safely upgrade after a conflicting commit
claim_assessment.evidence: Reader continued to observe a after another connection committed b; attempted UPDATE failed with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (517).

claim_assessment.claim: A long-lived reader can block a truncating checkpoint and retain WAL growth
claim_assessment.evidence: With reader held, WAL reached 824032 bytes and wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) returned [1,200,0]; after reader release it returned [0,0,0] and WAL size became 0.

claim_assessment.claim: SQLite 3.7.0-3.51.2 WAL reset/checkpoint race can corrupt a database
claim_assessment.evidence: No attempt was made to trigger the rare corruption race. This remains EXTERNAL_PRIMARY evidence from E1, not local reproduction.

counterhypothesis_update.before: SQLite locking may make explicit F2 contention/snapshot/checkpoint contracts unnecessary.
counterhypothesis_update.reason: The research harness directly observed typed contention and stale-snapshot failure modes plus checkpoint blockage under ordinary documented operations. Product-level handling remains necessary even when SQLite correctly enforces its own lock semantics.

confirmed_priorities: short read transactions plus generation/digest reentry
exact loaded SQLite version/config/topology binding before concurrency or durability credit

negative_evidence: Harness ran against local research SQLite 3.46.1, not the target F2 host/runtime dependency identity.
The 2026 WAL reset/checkpoint corruption race was not reproduced.
No power-loss durability experiment was run.
No F2 production module was modified or executed by this Trigger-6 experiment.
